explanation: Given only the non-tail node to delete, copy its successor’s data into it and bypass that successor. This deletes the selected value without needing a predecessor.
timeComplexity: O(1) callable time for one data copy and one link assignment; wrapper location takes O(index).
spaceComplexity: O(1), with no new list nodes.
attribution: Unmodified reference source: epi_judge_cpp_solutions/delete_node_from_list.cc. Elements of Programming Interviews Judge authors; repository LICENSE: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: The selected node now holds exactly the next value and points to the node after that value, producing the required deleted value sequence. The selected object remains reachable; its former successor object is bypassed, so this operation is value deletion rather than preserving the selected object’s value.
walkthrough: Case [7,5,9,2] selects zero-based position 1. The wrapper passes node 5; the callable writes 9 into that node and bypasses the old node 9. It returns no value; the wrapper sees [7,9,2].
edgeCases: The selected node cannot be the tail.
Selecting the head is permitted by this exercise.
The method intentionally changes the selected node’s stored value.
